title: Polymorphic Invocation Facade: SDK bindings for incremental outputs and deterministic tool replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
This ticket implements a small, language-agnostic 'InvocationFacade' abstraction and reference bindings in TypeScript, Python, and Go. Goals: 1) Provide a stable, simple API for incremental token/fragment emission, tool/function invocation, and structured output parsing. 2) Allow deterministic replay of tool calls for diagnostics and unit tests. 3) Offer compatibility adapters that map existing SDK shapes to the new facade with minimal client changes.

Background: Engineers using existing SDKs have diverging patterns for streaming and tool calls. We need a canonical, testable interface that supports: real-time chunked messages, tool invocation metadata, idempotent replay handles, and schema-typed structured events. This ticket covers design, PRs, and reference examples.
acceptance_criteria: Define a small facade type in TS/PY/Go that supports: startInvocation(), emitFragment(), callTool(), finishInvocation(), and replay(handle).
Reference implementations in TS/Python/Go committed to the mono-repo under sdk/adapters/* with unit tests.
Adapters to map legacy SDK streaming callbacks to the facade without breaking existing surface area.
Deterministic replay that can reconstruct tool call sequence and inputs for recorded sessions.
Performance overhead under 5% for typical latency-sensitive cases (benchmarked).
design_notes:
Key design decisions:
- Minimal core surface (5 ops) to maximize portability across languages.
- Tool calls return a ReplayHandle object (opaque string token) that can be used to re-execute or inspect calls.
- Use framed JSON events for streaming: every fragment is {type:string, seq:int, body: string|object, meta:object} serialized as line-delimited JSON to avoid custom binary framing.
- Structured outputs validated against lightweight schemas (JSON Schema v7) at emission time, but SDK adapters can operate in permissive mode (schema warnings).
- Backpressure contract: emitFragment is allowed to be called asynchronously; adapters expose an async drain() hook to coordinate batching.

Trade-offs:
- We avoid embedding heavy protobuf schemas to keep adapters lightweight. This may limit some binary-efficient paths but improves adoption.
- Deterministic replay requires recording deterministic RNG seeds and model variant identifiers; added metadata is included with every tool call.
api_examples:
Python example:

class InvocationFacade:
    def start_invocation(self, prompt: str, metadata: dict | None = None) -> str: ...
    async def emit_fragment(self, handle: str, fragment: dict) -> None: ...
    async def call_tool(self, handle: str, tool_name: str, input: dict) -> str: ...
    async def finish_invocation(self, handle: str, result_meta: dict | None = None) -> None: ...
    async def replay(self, token: str, mode: str = 'dry-run') -> dict: ...

# usage sketch
fac = InvocationFacadeImpl()
handle = fac.start_invocation('Extract action items')
await fac.emit_fragment(handle, {'type': 'text_chunk', 'body': 'Action: assign owner'})
replay_token = await fac.call_tool(handle, 'ticket.create', {'title': 'Fix logging'})
await fac.finish_invocation(handle)
await fac.replay(replay_token, mode='replay')

Go example:

type InvocationFacade interface {
    StartInvocation(prompt string, metadata map[string]string) (string, error)
    EmitFragment(handle string, fragment map[string]interface{}) error
    CallTool(handle string, toolName string, input map[string]interface{}) (string, error)
    FinishInvocation(handle string, meta map[string]interface{}) error
    Replay(token string, mode string) (map[string]interface{}, error)
}

// usage sketch
fac := NewInvocationFacade()
h, _ := fac.StartInvocation("Condense notes", nil)
fac.EmitFragment(h, map[string]interface{}{"type":"chunk","body":"line1"})
token, _ := fac.CallTool(h, "db.insert", map[string]interface{}{"row":{}})
fac.FinishInvocation(h, nil)
fac.Replay(token, "dry-run")
implementation_plan: 1) Spec: publish TS/PY/Go surface in SDK repo and internal RFC doc (Confluence link under links). 2) Implement TS reference (4d) + tests. 3) Implement Python reference (3d) + tests. 4) Implement Go reference (3d) + tests. 5) Adapter layer to map existing streaming callbacks to facade (2d). 6) Benchmarks and perf tuning (2d). 7) Docs and examples (2d). 8) Release behind feature flag and gather internal adoption (1 cycle).
testing_plan:
Unit tests for each binding cover:
- happy path incremental emission and finish
- tool call recorded metadata contains model id + seed
- replay reconstructs same tool-call sequence and inputs
- schema validation path rejects malformed structured output (and returns warning)
Integration tests:
- end-to-end: inbound request -> facade -> tool call -> persisted replay -> replay run returns identical call sequence
Performance tests:
- microbenchmarks for emitFragment latency with/without adapter
- memory overhead test when recording 10k-fragment sessions
comments: 2026-01-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Drafted core surface and acceptance criteria. Assigned to Diego for implementation.

2026-01-18 - Diego Martinez: Started TS reference. Chose line-delimited JSON framing to keep cross-language parity. Encountered ambiguity about sequence numbering when fragments arrive out-of-order from parallel generators.
2026-01-21 - Priya Rao (Design): Reviewed API sketches; requested adding 'meta.source' on fragments to identify tool vs model origin for UX mapping.
2026-01-26 - Diego Martinez: Implemented TS start/emit/call/finish in prototype. Added ReplayHandle that encodes base64-encoded JSON with metadata. Opening PR for early feedback.
2026-02-03 - SRE: Perf smoke test shows ~3.8% additional latency for small 128-token sessions when recording replay metadata (acceptable). Need metric tags to track in production.
2026-02-10 - PM (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize Python reference for customer SDKs; requested a migration guide for existing streaming clients.
